intro.text: An old kingdom of Nalthis that covered the lowlands of present-day Hallandren and the highlands of present-day Idris, until the Manywar split it in two.

description.text: Hanald held most of the lowlands, the Pahn Kahl keeping the rest, as well as the highlands, with the Bright Sea on its eastern side. The valley was mild, seldom cold or stormy, and easy to farm, while the colder mountains made farming harder. The Tears of Edgli grew nowhere but in its soil.

Its wealth grew quickly. As the only place the Tears of Edgli grew, it controlled the dye trade, and its jungles and mountains yielded goods found nowhere else. From its capital, the port of T'Telir, sea routes ran to lands such as Tedradel. The mountains held rich ore, among it the sole known source of copper anywhere, and carried trade roads north to Kuth and Huth.
A king or queen ruled. The first was Vo's wife, made queen after his death while carrying his child, and her descendants held the throne for three hundred years.

The royal family's home was a great black palace in T'Telir, stark and full of strange turns meant to confuse attackers. When a king died, his servants were killed so they could serve him in the afterlife.

items.text: Pahn Kahl fishing villages already dotted the region when ships from Chedesh, exploring the coasts, found the jungle valley. One explorer, Vo, died aboard a ship in the bay and became the first Returned. Paying the natives little heed, his crewmates founded Hanald there and chose his pregnant wife as their queen.

The kingdom spread fast across most of the lowlands and into the highlands, facing little resistance, since the only other lowland kingdom, Pahn Kahl, was weak. Its economy boomed on dye and other lowland crops, and mines were opened in the northern mountains, copper among them.

The royal family took a keen interest in Awakening, then a young art. The Five Scholars made many advances, such as making Lifeless from a single Breath and inventing ichor-alcohol, which let nations field far bigger and cheaper armies. With so many discoveries coming out of Hanald, its neighbours feared falling ever further behind.
When one of Hanald's Returned saw war in a vision, Hanald struck first against the other nations.
At first the royal family seemed to place a general at the head of a vast army, but the family soon fled T'Telir for the highlands.

In the Manywar that followed, Hanald's chief rivals, Kuth and Huth, were destroyed. Hallandren, named after the old kingdom, arose when Peacegiver began the line of God Kings, while the old royal line founded Idris in the mountains, leaving Hanald divided.
